thesis: The deterministic result supports Vertiv as a compounder with growth as a secondary fit. Structural AI power/cooling demand, strong customer economics, rising FCF/share and effective execution justify NORMAL status, while price near Base value, working-capital-assisted H1 cash flow and the unseasoned UIG acquisition argue for the mechanical 0-2% starting range rather than aggressive sizing. Macro pacing remains 0.8 and does not alter the company score.

evidence.claim: The completed core score is 75.38 with full 100% coverage; compounder and growth are eligible and all Hard Vetoes are cleared.
Locked DCF values are Bear $82.25, Base $240.42 and Bull $473.84 versus the $249.39 cutoff price.
Q2 sales grew 24.1% and operating profit 44.2% YoY, while full-year organic growth guidance was 30%-32%.
H1 OCF was $1.867B but included a $678.8M working-capital source, so current cash conversion requires normalization.
The signed UIG transaction requires about $1.45B upfront cash plus up to $1.15B contingent cash consideration.

counterevidence: Price is already slightly above locked Base value, so the case lacks a large initial valuation cushion.
Several growth vectors remain correlated to the same AI/hyperscaler capex cycle.
H1 cash flow benefits from working capital and should not be annualized mechanically.
UIG return on invested capital is unproven at the cutoff.
unknowns: Top-customer concentration and backlog cancellation profile.
UIG post-close ROIC and pro-forma leverage.
falsifiers: Normalized FCF/share misses the Base path for two years while retained capital and inventory continue rising.
Backlog/orders contract persistently while AI infrastructure spending remains healthy, indicating share or execution loss.
UIG earns sub-cost-of-capital returns or materially weakens the balance sheet without offsetting cash-flow growth.

key_kpis.name: UIG ROIC/net leverage
key_kpis.threshold: ROIC above cost of capital with controlled leverage
